title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as new satellite launches and funding initiatives take center stage. Meanwhile, concerns about the health of the ISS and geopolitical tensions in orbit remind us that not all is smooth sailing.

themes.title: Satellite Launches Abound
themes.body: Rocket Lab's recent launch of the 10th Synspective satellite underscores the growing demand for satellite services. This trend is further amplified by Spain's backing of FOSSA's sovereign communications initiative.

themes.title: Funding Fuels Space Ventures
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4B to space resilience is a clear indicator of the increasing prioritization of space defense. Additionally, True Anomaly's $190M Series C funding round highlights investor confidence in the commercial space sector.

themes.title: Geopolitical Tensions in Orbit
themes.body: Recent reports of Russian co-orbital activity near commercial GEO slots signal a potential escalation in space-related geopolitical maneuvering. As Europe grapples with security challenges in orbit, the implications for international cooperation are becoming more pronounced.

themes.title: Health of the ISS in Question
themes.body: The recent ISS repair spacewalk raises eyebrows about the station's long-term viability and operational integrity. As private entities like Sierra Space advance their own space capabilities, the future of the ISS may hinge on commercial partnerships.
